first:
You step onto the ferry and I ask you, "What is your name?" Nera Moss looks at me with a curious gaze. Her eyes are wide with excitement but also reserved curiosity.

"Your name is Nera Moss," she says, her voice barely above a whisper. She takes out her watch from her pocket and turns it around, feeling the movement of the water as if she were part of the ocean's rhythm. Her eyes move back to mine, revealing the vastness of the harbor beyond.

"The blue cord is for me," she says, her tone serious. I nod, feeling a sense of calm that has been lost in this strange place. It is not until we have walked through the docks of Bellwether that we realize that we have arrived here by chance. 

We board our boat, take off our life jackets, and proceed to Nera Moss' ferry. We stare at the horizon as the tide pulls us closer, making the small town feel like an endless stretch of water. The silence between us is thick, and we can hear the waves lapping against the shore, their sound echoing deep into the distance. Our paths cross every day on this journey, yet each time we meet again, we still find ourselves in this spot.

As we navigate the waters, we come across the fishing boats of Bellwether, their hands gently grasping the ropes while they follow the currents. Suddenly, we see a tall figure on the horizon, his face obscured by fog, but he can be seen ahead. His eyes darting nervously, I look away from him, my mind searching for clues about who he might be. As we pass, we see a small sailboat passing, its sails fluttering lightly, and I'm drawn to him, my heart racing. He seems to know something about us, as if he could read minds. I look back to Nera Moss, who nods to me, and she too sees what I'm looking for.

From this moment forward, we become one, and we're only apart by the last word. Our journey continues, and we soon arrive on the ferry, feeling the sea breeze in our hair. I look around, and I'm surprised by how much there is to explore, even after so many years, after living so long in the past, even more so now, when we are sailing under the sky, crossing oceans, exploring new territories, all the way up to the edge of our own world.

You asked for the blue cord, and I stepped onto her ferry. Your knowledge of her surroundings is unparalleled, and I am as curious about this world as you are.
"Your friend," I said, stepping forward into the harbor. "This is your guide."
"You have arrived, I believe, on a journey we must embark upon together," I continued, gently pushing myself through the water. The silence was thick with anticipation, yet I felt an immense sense of comfort in Nera's presence.
"Do not ask me questions, or else I will step between us, blocking your path," she murmured, her voice echoing from deep within the harbor. I hesitated, feeling the tension in the air around me. It was difficult to say no when we were so close together.
The harbor had changed, but I couldn't help but feel its magic lingered. Nera Moss had been here before, and I couldn’t imagine leaving without questioning her wisdom. She spoke of the secrets passed down by the locals, and the memories that lived in their bones. I felt like I was part of something greater than the world I knew, and it was hard to resist the pull of her words.
As we traveled along the harbor, we encountered the first few of the town, but they didn't know what we were talking about. We continued along the waterside, until we reached our destination - Bellwether. I was taken aback by the distance, yet I could tell that the harbor wasn't too far away. I wondered how long it would take to get there, and I was filled with curiosity for what awaited at that distant horizon.
We arrived, and I took off my harness, readying myself for the challenge ahead. Nera Moss was there, waiting for me; I could see her eyes reflecting the ocean, looking out over the vast expanse. As I approached her, I felt her warmth surrounding me, and I felt like I was truly part of her. My heart raced with excitement as I turned towards her, hoping to catch a glimpse of the future.
As we sailed toward the horizon, I couldn't help but wonder what the sea had returned. I saw the depths of the ocean, the vastness of the ocean, and the endless possibilities of what lay beyond it. Nera Moss was right, though, the sky looked different, and the stars seemed brighter than ever before. Her gaze was lost in the distance, and I felt a strange sense of peace settle over me. It was as if we were walking into a world of infinite possibility, and we were all in it, floating aimlessly along the water's edge.
